hyperedges.label: Expo Go limitation to development build workflow

nodes.label: Active graphify graph consultation directive
nodes.rationale: Requiring active graph queries instead of memory keeps the agent grounded in the extracted repository knowledge graph rather than assumptions.

nodes.label: Yostin (mobile app agent persona)
nodes.rationale: Defined as the agent used for mobile applications in Expo Go and Flutter that actively consults the graphify graph, scoping agent specialization to mobile work in this repo.

nodes.label: EAS cloud build, submit and OTA updates
nodes.norm_label: eas cloud build, submit and ota updates
nodes.rationale: Use EAS (build, submit, update) so no local Xcode or Android Studio is required; CLI is invoked as bunx eas-cli or npx eas-cli@latest, substituting for bare `eas` in docs examples.

nodes.label: Development build fallback for native code
nodes.norm_label: development build fallback for native code
nodes.rationale: After adding a library with native code, build locally with npx expo run:ios|android or in the cloud with eas build --profile development.

nodes.label: Expo Go limited to bundled native modules
nodes.norm_label: expo go limited to bundled native modules
nodes.rationale: Expo Go ships only its bundled native modules, so any library with native code forces a development build; this is the cost that motivates preferring recommended Expo modules over third-party libraries.

nodes.label: Expo Router file-based navigation in src/app
nodes.norm_label: expo router file-based navigation in src/app
nodes.rationale: Mandates Expo Router for all navigation: every file in src/app/ is a screen, _layout.tsx files define navigators, and non-route code (components, hooks, utils) must live outside src/app/ to keep the route tree clean.

nodes.label: Run lint and typecheck before declaring a task done
nodes.norm_label: run lint and typecheck before declaring a task done
nodes.rationale: Completion gate: npx expo lint plus npx tsc --noEmit must pass, with npx expo-doctor used to diagnose dependency and config issues.

nodes.label: create-expo-app starter scaffold
nodes.rationale: Project originates from create-expo-app, which explains the generic starter README and the npm install / npx expo start onboarding path.

nodes.label: Expo Go as a limited sandbox
nodes.norm_label: expo go as a limited sandbox
nodes.rationale: Expo Go is described as a limited sandbox for trying out app development, listed alongside development builds, Android emulator, and iOS simulator as run targets.

nodes.label: File-based routing via src/app
nodes.rationale: Development starts by editing files inside src/app because the template uses file-based routing (Expo Router).

nodes.label: reset-project script
nodes.rationale: npm run reset-project moves the starter code into an example directory and creates a blank src/app, so template demo code can be discarded without deleting it.

nodes.label: CLAUDE.md (@AGENTS.md include)
nodes.rationale: Contains only the @AGENTS.md import so Claude-based tooling shares a single source of agent instructions instead of duplicating them.

nodes.label: Ask before every code change
nodes.rationale: Mandates asking the user before each change or modification so edits stay user-approved; trade-off is slower iteration in exchange for control.

nodes.label: Continuous Native Generation (do not hand-edit ios/android)
nodes.norm_label: continuous native generation (do not hand-edit ios/android)
nodes.rationale: If ios/ and android/ do not exist they are generated, so manual edits would be lost or conflict; native behavior must be configured through app.json and config plugins instead.

nodes.label: Always use npx expo install for dependencies
nodes.norm_label: always use npx expo install for dependencies
nodes.rationale: npm/yarn/pnpm/bun add do not resolve SDK-compatible versions; expo install and `expo install --fix` keep the dependency set aligned with the installed Expo SDK.

nodes.label: Do not trust training data: fetch versioned Expo docs
nodes.norm_label: do not trust training data: fetch versioned expo docs
nodes.rationale: Expo ships breaking changes every SDK release, so remembered APIs are likely renamed, moved, or removed. Workflow: read the expo major version in package.json, fetch https://docs.expo.dev/versions/v<major>.0.0/ plus the llms.txt doc index (which corrects common LLM misconceptions), and never answer from memory.

nodes.label: Prefer recommended Expo modules over third-party libraries
nodes.norm_label: prefer recommended expo modules over third-party libraries
nodes.rationale: Recommended Expo modules are SDK-compatible and available in Expo Go, avoiding unnecessary development builds; check available skills before adding dependencies.
